'''Jordin T. Kare''' (October 24, 1956 – July 19, 2017) was an American [[physicist]] and [[aerospace engineer]] who researched [[laser propulsion]]. He was responsible for Mockingbird,<ref name="Mockingbird">[https://web.archive.org/web/20131006210340/http://www.quantumg.net/mockingbird.pdf Mockingbird]</ref> a conceptual design for an extremely small (75&nbsp;kg [[dry mass]]) reusable launch vehicle, and was involved in the [[Clementine mission|Clementine lunar mapping mission]].<ref name="IntersectionPeopleJK">{{cite web |url=http://www.johnbray.org.uk/intersection/people.html#Jordin%20Kare |title=Intersection Science Programme Participants: Jordin Kare |accessdate=2007-08-13 |author=Jordin Kare |website=Intersection Science Programme Participants |publisher=John Bray |archive-date=2012-02-07 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120207011305/http://www.johnbray.org.uk/intersection/people.html#Jordin%20Kare |url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name="cc05jk">{{Cite web|url=http://www.capclave.org/capclave05/participants.php#JordinKare|title=Capclave 2005: Confirmed Program Participants|website=www.capclave.org|access-date=2016-08-30}}</ref>
Kare also conceived the ''SailBeam'' interstellar propulsion technique. In the [[science fiction]] [[Fandom|fan community]], he was a composer, performer and recording artist of [[filk music]].

==Early life and education==
Kare grew up in the Philadelphia area and attended [[Harriton High School]] in [[Rosemont, Pennsylvania]]. He received his [[Bachelor of Science|B.S.]] in  [[electrical engineering]] and [[physics]] from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1978 and [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]] in [[astrophysics]] from the [[University of California, Berkeley]] in 1984.<ref name="IntersectionPeopleJK" /><ref name="sau93">{{cite web
|url        = http://www.space-access.org/updates/sau93.html
|title      = Space Access Update #93
|accessdate = 2007-08-13
|date       = 2000-04-13
|publisher  = [[Space Access Society]]
}}
</ref>

Kare was the brother of [[Susan Kare]], designer of the fonts and icons of the original [[Apple Macintosh]] user interface.<ref name="monellw2003" /><ref>{{cite web|url=http://library.stanford.edu/mac/primary/interviews/kare/index.html|title=Interview with Susan Kare|date=2001-02-19|publisher=[[Stanford University]]|accessdate=2007-08-13|author=Alex Soojung-Kim Pang|work=Making the Macintosh|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20100311195002/http://library.stanford.edu/mac/primary/interviews/kare/index.html|archivedate=2010-03-11}}
</ref>

==Career==
Kare worked for many years at [[Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory]] (LLNL).  In 1996, he left LLNL and, after working briefly for a small space-related startup company, in 1997 became an independent consultant specializing in advanced space system design,<ref name="sau93" /> and started his own company.<ref name="monellw2003">{{cite web
 |url          = http://www.monell.org/Newsletters/Monell_Fall03.pdf
 |title        = The Monell Connection, Winter 2003
 |accessdate   = 2007-08-13
 |year         = 2003
 |publisher    = [[Monell Chemical Senses Center]]
 |pages        = 9
 |archive-date = 2008-04-07
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20080407124004/http://www.monell.org/Newsletters/Monell_Fall03.pdf
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref>

===Laser propulsion===
He was a leading advocate of [[laser propulsion]] for space launch and in-space propulsion. He organized a 1986 workshop on laser propulsion at LLNL and later led a development program for ground to orbit laser launch supported by [[Strategic Defense Initiative Organization|SDIO]].  He received a [[NASA Institute for Advanced Concepts]] grant to study a near-term form of laser launch using arrays of relatively low-powered lasers.<ref name="sau93" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.islandone.org/Propulsion/JordinKareBiblio.html|title=Jordin Kare Laser Launch Bibliography|website=www.islandone.org|access-date=2016-08-30}}</ref><ref>{{cite web
|url=http://www.niac.usra.edu/files/studies/final_report/897Kare.pdf
|title = Modular Laser Launch Architecture: Analysis and Beam Module Design. Final Report.
|accessdate = 2007-08-12
|author = Dr. Jordin T. Kare
|date = 2004-05-18
|publisher = Kare Technical Consulting
}}</ref><ref>{{cite news| url=http://www.foxnews.com/scitech/2011/01/25/nasa-exploring-lasers-beams-zap-rockets-outer-space/ | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110127183155/http://www.foxnews.com/scitech/2011/01/25/nasa-exploring-lasers-beams-zap-rockets-outer-space/ | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 27, 2011 | work=Fox News | title=NASA Exploring Laser Beams to Zap Rockets Into Outer Space | date=2011-01-25}}</ref>  He co-founded [[LaserMotive]], Inc., a laser power beaming entrant in the [[Elevator:2010#Beam Power Challenge|Elevator:2010 Beam Power Challenge]], in 2006,<ref name="lasermotive bio">[http://lasermotive.com/about/executive-staff/jordin-kare/ Jordin Kare] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120629103333/http://lasermotive.com/about/executive-staff/jordin-kare/ |date=2012-06-29 }} (bio at Lasermotive site). Retrieved Aug. 3, 2017.</ref> and led the overall system design and the laser transmitter design efforts.

===Sailbeam===
Kare proposed the SailBeam Boosted Magsail in a report prepared for NASA's Institute for Advanced Concepts called "High-Acceleration Micro-Scale Laser Sails for Interstellar Propulsion".<ref>[http://www.niac.usra.edu/files/studies/final_report/597Kare.pdf "High-Acceleration Micro-Scale Laser Sails for Interstellar Propulsion"]</ref> A key idea is that if vast numbers of tiny sails are used to accelerate rather than one enormous one, the same amount of mass can be brought to high speeds with a less complex optical system.  Unlike particle-beam propulsion, in which the beam disperses as it travels, a stream of low-mass microsails is not limited by such diffraction.  By using dielectric rather than metal sails, the sails can also be accelerated much closer to their power source. The stream of microsails then becomes a source of propulsion to a starship as particle beams mounted on the starship vaporize the incoming sails into plasma.

==Filk music and science fiction==
Kare was also a [[science fiction]] [[science fiction fandom|fan]] and [[filk music|filksinger]].<ref name="fangallery"/> He was a regular attendee and program participant at [[science fiction convention]]s starting in 1975.<ref name="cu22bio" /><ref name="cc05jk" /> He was an editor of ''The Westerfilk Collection: Songs of Fantasy and Science Fiction'', an important filksong collection, and later a partner in [[Off Centaur Publications]], the first commercial publisher specializing in filk songbooks and recordings.<ref name="cu22bio" /><ref name="fangallery">{{Cite web
 |url          = http://www.scifiinc.net/scifiinc/gallery/bio/Kare,_Jordin.htm
 |title        = Jordin Kare
 |work         = Fan Gallery
 |publisher    = SCIFI Inc.
 |date         = August 2014
 |accessdate   = 2017-08-03
 |archive-date = 2012-02-05
 |archive-url  = https://web.archive.org/web/20120205184547/http://www.scifiinc.net/scifiinc/gallery/bio/Kare,_Jordin.htm
 |url-status   = dead
}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web <!-- Citation bot no -->|url=http://www.librarything.de/work/1522010|title=The Westerfilk Collection: Songs of Fantasy and Science Fiction |edition=2nd |date=May 1981 |publisher=von Off Centaur Publications|website=LibraryThing.com|access-date=2016-08-30}}</ref><ref name="singout">{{Cite web|url=http://www.interfilk.org/interfilk/singout.htm|title=Filk music?|publisher=singitout.org|accessdate=2007-08-13|author=Jordin Kare|url-status=dead|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20070731100240/http://www.interfilk.org//interfilk/singout.htm|archivedate=2007-07-31}}</ref>  Kare won two [[Pegasus Award]]s for his filk songs, Best Classic Filk Song in 2010 for "Fire in the Sky" and Best Writer/Composer in 2017, as well as seven additional nominations from 1987 onwards.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://ovff.org/pegasus/people/jordin-kare.html|work=Ohio Valley Filk Fest|title=Jordin Kare|date=2017-10-21|accessdate=2017-11-06}}</ref>

An astrophysicist character with his name appears in ''[[War of Honor]]'' and ''[[Torch of Freedom]]'', military science fiction novels in the ''[[Honor Harrington]]'' series by [[David Weber]].  A physicist by his name (and his wife, Mary Kay) appear in ''Callahan's Touch'' by [[Spider Robinson]], where he shoots a [[Clurichaun|cluricaune]] with a fire extinguisher. His song "Fire in the Sky" is featured in the novel ''[[Fallen Angels (science fiction novel)|Fallen Angels]]'' by [[Larry Niven]], [[Jerry Pournelle]], and [[Michael Flynn (writer)|Michael Flynn]] and a cover by [[S. J. Tucker|S.J Tucker]] with a bridge by Kristoph Klover appears on the 2025 album ''The Pegasus Nominees, Vol. 1: Songs Of Space, Science & Science Fiction.''

==Death==
In June 2017, Kare's wife Mary Kay announced via Twitter that his [[aortic valve]] was failing and would be [[aortic valve replacement|replaced]].<ref name=TwitterJune21>[https://twitter.com/MKKare/status/877563001401778176 People have said they didn't see my earlier posts so reposting. Jordin's aortic valve is failing. He is having surgery June 28 to replace...], by Mary Kay Kare, on Twitter; published June 21, 2017; retrieved July 19, 2017</ref> On July 19, she announced that he had died.<ref name=Twitter>[https://twitter.com/MKKare/status/887830761495298048 Jordin's heart stopped is pm & could not be restarted. He's gone. I am having him cremated here & will take him home asap.], by Mary Kay Kare; published July 19, 2017; retrieved July 19, 2017</ref>
